subject: Materials Science
title: What Makes an Alloy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: What Makes an Alloy.

hook.text: Pure gold is too soft for rings. Pure iron rusts away. Neither works alone.

buildup.text: An alloy mixes two or more elements, with at least one being a metal.

discovery.text: Foreign atoms distort the crystal lattice, blocking the slip that makes pure metals soft.

twist.text: Bronze — copper plus tin — was so transformative it named an entire era of history.

climax.text: Today engineers tune alloys atom by atom, designing properties no pure metal can match.

punchline.text: Alloys exist because no pure metal is good enough.

quiz.question: Why are alloys generally harder than pure metals?
options: Foreign atoms block slip planes in the crystal
Mixing metals removes the crystal structure
